#### What is Battle of the Books After Hours?
Battle of the Books After Hours is an adults-only reading competition.
Teams of 3-5 will read 6 preselected books (see booklist below)and then join in a trivia competition at Flood Zone Brewery (October 7) or 1623 Brewing Co. (October 21 & 28).

Check out books from the booklist below or purchase from Park Books on Main.The competition will have two rounds of 20 questions in multiple formats:fill-in-the-blank, true or false, or multiple choice.
Doors open at 5:30pm to practice and purchase food and beverages.Teams will be sent full competition rules in advance.
If you are interested in participating but do not have a team, email greatreads@carr.org, as soon as possible.
*   Teams of 3-5 can sign up.
Please note we have limited ticket quantities for each team size due to venue capacity.
*   Cost is $15 per person ($45 for a 3 person team, $60 for a 4 person team, and $75 for a 5 person team).
*   The team size you sign up for is the team size you are committing to.
Expect that no additional team members will be able to be added.
*   Registration opens June 10.
If registration is full, you can join the wait list through the registration form.
*   Please note that on the night of the event, you may be seated at the same table as another team.
We will try our best to work with teams and seating arrangements so that there is spacing, but this may be necessary.
*   Please only register your team for one night to allow more teams the chance to participate.
#### Presented by Park Books on Main, 1623 Brewing Co., Flood Zone Brewery, and Carroll County Public Library.

It’s time for pumpkin and squash visitors in our gardens to smile and wink their way into our hearts again.
Their trailing vines and giant happy green leaves now take a well-earned rest in the cool autumn mornings.
The Carroll Garden Club, along with CCPL's Finksburg Branch, will provide program participants with the opportunity to see a collection of happy pumpkins and squash.
Learn how these bumpy, sometimes lumpy, colorful fruits have brought smiles to the faces of anyone lucky enough to become friends with one of them.
Children will learn firsthand the characteristics and uses of these happy visitors.

They will also create wild and crazy pumpkin and squash ‘garden beings’ using found natural materials from the forest floor, our vegetable and flower gardens, and even bits and pieces from Grandma’s sewing basket.
A show-and-tell will round out the activity, with each child sharing the story of their exciting pumpkin or squash friend.
Their new friend will travel home with them to celebrate a wondrous new season of great pumpkins and squash.

Join guest speaker Paul Ruehs, a local history adjunct instructor, as he takes us through the musical genre that we call rock and roll.
We’ll explore its inception in the late '40s and '50s and learn what rock and roll is and how it differs from pop and other musical genres.
We’ll also learn about the men, women, and organizations who helped found the genre.
Then we'll discuss how musical influences from the '60s and '70s affected rock and roll.
Finally, we’ll look at how this popular music has changed over the decades.

This two-part series offers an overview of the U.S. Intelligence Community (IC) from World War I to the present.

It covers three main areas: (1) a brief history of espionage and the post-World War II reorganization of U.S. spy agencies, (2) an examination of the IC, including its member agencies, their roles, and methods, and (3) a study of counterintelligence, focusing on insider threats, their motivations, espionage activities, and the resulting damage.
Paul Ruehs is a seasoned security professional with over 45 years of experience in national security, law enforcement, and counterintelligence.
He has served in both military and civilian roles, including 25 years in the USAF Security Police and leadership positions within the Department of Energy and Defense Intelligence Agency.

He is a certified trainer with over 10,000 hours of classroom instruction, teaching at institutions like Carroll Community College and McDaniel College, and is a recognized expert in Operations Security (OPSEC), contributing to interagency panels and national symposiums.
Holding a B.S. in History & Political Science and an M.A. in National Security Studies, Paul is also a published co-author and remains actively engaged in academic and security communities.
